steps: Treat the cause and slow progression: control BP (ACEi/ARB if albuminuric), glycaemic control, SGLT2 inhibitor where indicated.
Reduce cardiovascular risk (statin, lifestyle, smoking cessation); avoid nephrotoxins; dose-adjust drugs.
Manage complications — anaemia (iron ± ESA), CKD-mineral-bone disorder (phosphate, vitamin D), acidosis, hyperkalaemia.
Monitor eGFR/ACR; vaccinate; dietary sodium/protein advice.
Plan renal replacement / transplant and refer nephrology as eGFR declines.

drugRefs.why: First-line for albuminuric CKD/hypertension — reduces proteinuria and slows progression; monitor K⁺ and creatinine after initiation.
Slows CKD progression and reduces cardiovascular/renal events in albuminuric CKD (diabetic and non-diabetic).
KDIGO recommends statin therapy in adults with CKD to reduce cardiovascular risk.

Treats secondary hyperparathyroidism/vitamin D deficiency in CKD-MBD.
